findings.title: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no argument; services does not compile
findings.body: `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` calls a zero-argument overload. The only definition in the repository is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 (grep for the name finds no other definition). The services module therefore fails to compile, and nothing in this PR can be built or tested. The predicate is meant to be passkeys-enabled only (the comment above it says 'skip the form when user is re-authenticating' unless passkeys are on), so the fix is the one in the next finding: make the method take no argument and check only `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) returns false when no user is set, which removes passkey data from the first login page and from the invalid-username path
findings.body: The old code filled webauthn data only when `context.getUser() == null` (base lines 110-112 inside the else branch; base challenge(error, field) at line 136). The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, so the condition is inverted for the no-user case. Concretely: (1) authenticate() at lines 114-117 with user null (ordinary login page) no longer calls fillContextForm, so ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI is not set; login.ftl:16 and login-username.ftl:22 then render autocomplete='username' instead of 'username webauthn', and the conditional passkey block in passkeys.ftl:2 is skipped. (2) challenge(error, field) at lines 136-141 is reached with user null on an invalid username (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:109 testInvalidUser) and no longer fills. The PR's own tests assert the opposite: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:145 and :195, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:183, :190 and :241, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:192 and :250 all expect 'username webauthn' on the first page. Those assertions would fail. The re-authentication path (user set) is the only case the new code handles. The fix is to drop the user parameter and the `user != null` clause so that the helper means 'passkeys enabled', which also resolves the compile error above. Callers at lines 115 and 137 then fill in both cases, as the tests expect.

findings.title: After a wrong password on the username-then-password flow, PasswordForm now renders passkey data, but its first render does not
findings.body: PasswordForm extends UsernamePasswordForm and is constructed with a session (PasswordForm.java:35-37), so webauthnAuth is non-null. PasswordForm.authenticate() (PasswordForm.java:45-52) renders the password page without calling fillContextForm. The error path, however, goes through challenge(context, error, field) (UsernamePasswordForm.java:136-141), and with the user set it now fills the passkey data. A wrong password on that page therefore shows passkey data that the first render did not. No test in this PR covers PasswordForm. Is that intended? If not, PasswordForm should override the error path as it already overrides authenticate().

findings.title: NoSuchElementException import is unused after the assertThrows lines were replaced
findings.body: The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls (base lines 199 and 210) were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., notNullValue())`. Grep finds no other use of `NoSuchElementException` in this file, so the import at line 51 is dead.

findings.title: PasswordCredentialModel is imported but never used in this file
findings.body: The import at line 35 is not referenced anywhere in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java (grep finds only the import). Remove it.

findings.title: Negative webauthn checks catch every Exception, so they pass on any driver error
findings.body: In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey (lines 291-296 and 312-317), the absence of the webauthn form is checked with `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { }`. Any exception from findElement passes the check, including a stale element or a session error, so the assertion does not prove the form is absent. A check such as `driver.findElements(By.xpath(...)).isEmpty()` would assert what the comment says, and the existing `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` pattern in PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:202 is narrower.

findings.title: Re-authentication no longer skips the username form for every user when passkeys are enabled, not just for users with a passkey
findings.body: Before this PR, UsernameForm skipped the form on re-authentication (context.success() at line 50) unless the user had linked brokers. With `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (once the predicate is fixed to be passkeys-only), the skip is also disabled for password-only users in a passkey-enabled realm. The new tests cover re-authentication with passkeys enabled only for users with a passkey (PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:259-321) and the no-passkey case only with passkeys disabled at realm level (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:277-333). A password-only user in a passkey-enabled realm is not covered. Is it intended that such a user now sees the username form on prompt=login?

summary: Two blockers. (1) UsernameForm.java:47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no argument, but the only definition takes a UserModel (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160). services does not compile. (2) The same helper returns false when no user is set, which inverts the old 'user == null' gate. The first login page and the invalid-username path lose the conditional-UI passkey data (ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI), so autocomplete reverts to 'username'. The PR's own tests expect 'username webauthn' on the first page (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:145, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:183) and would fail. Dropping the user parameter so the helper means 'passkeys enabled' fixes both. The re-authentication path (user set) works as the tests expect. Other findings: a question on PasswordForm error pages getting passkey data that the first render lacks, two unused imports, a weak negative assertion in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey, and a question on whether password-only users on passkey realms should still skip the username form on re-auth. Nothing was built or run; all checks are by reading and grep.
